newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Papua New Guinea seeking to boost copra output.
newsitem.headline: Papua New Guinea seeking to boost copra output.

text.p: Papua New Guinea is aiming to expand the output of copra from its coconut trees to two million tonnes by 2005 from the current 150,000 tonnes, the general manager of its Copra Marketing Board (CMB) said on Friday.

Joseph Bae said in a report to an edible oil markets meeting in Singapore that the CMB wants to spread the use of high yielding hybrid coconut trees among the 65,000 small farm holders scattered in the eight main coconut-producing provinces.
"We need to encourage present as well as past growers to deliver more copra to us from existing trees in the short term," he said.
Bae said they must also eradicate the rhinoceros beetle and black palm weevil which attack and kill young coconut plants.
"Funding and research staff have been provided by the European Union to find a method of control," he said.
